title: Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE — Premium Revision Paper #14

pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #14
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which tongue twister helps you practise /f/ and /v/? (1 mark)
   A. Twin Tom twists ten twigs.
   B. Dina's dad did a dance.
   C. Ten tired tigers took Tom's toys.
   D. Five fat frogs fried five fine fish.

2. A person in your family who lived long before your grandparents is an (1 mark)
   A. elder
   B. orphan
   C. widow
   D. ancestor

3. 'I saw a goat. ___ goat was brown.' Which article fits the blank? (1 mark)
   A. A
   B. An
   C. The
   D. Some

4. Which sentence uses 'the' correctly for a best one? (1 mark)
   A. She is tall the girl.
   B. She is a the tallest girl.
   C. She is tallest a girl.
   D. She is the tallest girl.

5. What is a surname? (1 mark)
   A. Your school
   B. Your family name
   C. Your address
   D. Your first name

6. What should you do if a question does not apply to you? (1 mark)
   A. Tear the form
   B. Leave it empty
   C. Write a false answer
   D. Write N/A or draw a line

7. Poems and similes: Which is a simile? (1 mark)
   A. She sang like a bird.
   B. She sang loudly.
   C. She is a bird.
   D. She sang.

8. Which noun is always plural? (1 mark)
   A. cup
   B. book
   C. scissors
   D. spoon

9. Why should there be a gap between words? (1 mark)
   A. To use more paper
   B. To hide mistakes
   C. So that the words are easy to read
   D. To make the page dirty

10. An underpass is (1 mark)
   A. a bicycle
   B. a kind of train
   C. a bridge over a river
   D. a path or road that goes under a busy road

11. What does 'bleed' mean? (1 mark)
   A. To sing
   B. To eat too much
   C. To sleep
   D. To lose blood from a cut

12. On a map, the four main directions are (1 mark)
   A. north, south, east and west
   B. front, back, near and far
   C. red, blue, green and yellow
   D. up, down, left and right

13. Pronouns: Choose the correct sentence. (1 mark)
   A. The nurse helped mine.
   B. The nurse helped my.
   C. The nurse helped me.
   D. The nurse helped I.

14. Complete: 'Give the book to ___.' (Ann and Eve) (1 mark)
   A. them
   B. they
   C. theirs
   D. their

15. Why should you use a mobile phone only with permission? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the battery last longer
   B. It keeps you safe and responsible
   C. It makes calls cheaper
   D. Phones are only for adults to own

16. Which word begins the greeting in a friendly letter? (1 mark)
   A. Yours
   B. Faithfully
   C. Dear
   D. Sincerely

17. Which is an example of extensive reading? (1 mark)
   A. Reading many story books in your free time
   B. Reading one line for a test
   C. Writing a letter
   D. Learning a poem for an exam

18. Why should you return borrowed books on time? (1 mark)
   A. So others can read them too
   B. To make the book dirty
   C. Because books are heavy
   D. To forget the title

19. Which is the comparative form of 'little' (amount)? (1 mark)
   A. least
   B. more little
   C. less
   D. littler

20. Which phrase is a better word for 'nice' food? (1 mark)
   A. delicious
   B. cold
   C. bad
   D. hard

21. Which word helps to show order in a narrative? (1 mark)
   A. eleven
   B. blue
   C. table
   D. suddenly

22. What should Neema do if a message frightens her? (1 mark)
   A. Reply
   B. Keep it secret
   C. Show a grown-up at once
   D. Share her password

23. In the safety dialogue, why did the message say 'You have won a prize'? (1 mark)
   A. To teach spelling
   B. It was a trick to steal information
   C. To reward Neema
   D. To help her homework

24. Quantifiers: Which sentence is correct? (1 mark)
   A. I do not have some money.
   B. I do not any have money.
   C. I do not have any money.
   D. I do not have many money.

25. Which is NOT a good way to run a reading club? (1 mark)
   A. Meet at a regular time
   B. Keep a list of books read
   C. Take turns to speak
   D. Everyone talks at once

26. Which is a good strategy for improving fluency? (1 mark)
   A. Reading each word very slowly with long stops
   B. Re-reading the same passage several times
   C. Skipping hard words
   D. Reading only the pictures

27. What is reader's theatre? (1 mark)
   A. Reading parts from a script with only your voice, without costumes or sets
   B. Silent reading
   C. Copying a script
   D. Acting a play with full costumes

28. Which sentence uses the right word for how she sings? (1 mark)
   A. She sings good.
   B. She sings goodly.
   C. She sings well.
   D. She sing well.

29. Which is an adverb of time meaning 'not at any time'? (1 mark)
   A. never
   B. usually
   C. often
   D. sometimes

30. Which sentence is punctuated correctly? (1 mark)
   A. We bought, rice beans and maize.
   B. We bought rice, beans and maize.
   C. We bought rice, beans, and, maize.
   D. We bought rice beans and maize.

31. Which is a polite way to interrupt a speaker? (1 mark)
   A. Excuse me, may I ask a question?
   B. You are wrong!
   C. Stop talking!
   D. Be quiet!

32. What should a person with diarrhoea do? (1 mark)
   A. Share their cup
   B. Stop drinking water
   C. Stay away from clean water
   D. Drink plenty of safe water and see a health worker

33. Which sentence is joined correctly? (1 mark)
   A. We swept the floor, for we wiped the desks.
   B. We swept the floor, nor we wiped the desks.
   C. We swept the floor, yet we wiped the desks.
   D. We swept the floor, and we wiped the desks.

34. What is the full set of coordinating conjunctions? (1 mark)
   A. in, on, at, by, to, from, with
   B. for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so
   C. if, when, while, since, until, unless, after
   D. he, she, it, we, you, they, I

35. After 'does' or 'did', which form of the main verb do we use? (1 mark)
   A. The plural form
   B. The -ing form
   C. The base form
   D. The past participle

36. What does 'A stitch in time saves nine' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Sewing is always fun
   B. Fixing a small problem early prevents a bigger one
   C. Time is money
   D. Nine stitches are better than one

37. What is the past participle of 'write'? (1 mark)
   A. writed
   B. written
   C. wrote
   D. writing

38. What is a fine? (1 mark)
   A. Money paid as a punishment for breaking a rule
   B. A payment for a service
   C. A kind of salary
   D. A gift of money

39. Which preposition shows movement to the inside? (1 mark)
   A. into
   B. beside
   C. on
   D. behind

40. Which word is a preposition of position? (1 mark)
   A. under
   B. run
   C. quickly
   D. happy

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Write a short dialogue of four lines in which you borrow a book from a friend politely. (4 marks)

42. Give three safety rules for using the internet. (4 marks)

43. Write two sentences using a simile of your own about a celebration. (4 marks)

44. Explain what 'prevention' means and use it in a sentence. (3 marks)

45. Write three ways to make your speech clearer. (3 marks)

46. Arrange in order: (a) Then she paid. (b) Grace entered the shop. (c) Finally, she went home. (2 marks)

47. Arrange in alphabetical order: goat, cow, hen, dog. (2 marks)

48. Explain why gestures should match your words. (2 marks)

49. Why is it important to interpret road signs correctly? (2 marks)

50. Sort these adverbs into manner, time and place: quietly, later, nearby, always, neatly, upstairs. (3 marks)

51. Rewrite in the plural: 'The child put a loaf and a tomato in the box.' (3 marks)

52. Explain how intonation can change the meaning of 'Really?' (3 marks)

53. Name the five senses and say why a descriptive writer uses them. (3 marks)

54. Explain the difference in meaning between 'hopping' and 'hoping'. Use each in a sentence. (3 marks)

55. Name the three groups of food on a healthy plate and give one example of each. (3 marks)

56. Change these adjectives into adverbs: gentle, angry, quick. (3 marks)

57. Explain what we learn from the story about honesty. (3 marks)

58. Write two words with the sound /uː/ and two words with /ʊ/. (2 marks)

59. Write the -ing form of: run, sit, swim. (3 marks)

60. Explain what word stress is. Give one example. (2 marks)

61. Use the words 'sibling', 'relative' and 'chore' in three sentences about a family. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #14 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Five fat frogs fried five fine fish.
   Five, fat, frogs, fried and fine have /f/ and five has /v/.

2. D — ancestor
   Ancestors are family members from long ago.

3. C — The
   The goat has already been mentioned, so we use the.

4. D — She is the tallest girl.
   We use the before superlative words such as tallest.

5. B — Your family name
   The surname is the family name.

6. D — Write N/A or draw a line
   N/A means not applicable and shows that you did not forget.

7. A — She sang like a bird.
   Like a bird compares her singing to a bird's.

8. C — scissors
   Scissors are two blades joined together, so the noun is plural.

9. C — So that the words are easy to read
   Gaps make the writing legible.

10. D — a path or road that goes under a busy road
   Pedestrians can walk through it without meeting cars.

11. D — To lose blood from a cut
   A bleeding wound loses blood.

12. A — north, south, east and west
   These are called the cardinal points.

13. C — The nurse helped me.
   Me is the object form of I.

14. A — them
   Them is the object form of they.

15. B — It keeps you safe and responsible
   A trusted adult can guide you.

16. C — Dear
   Friendly letters begin with Dear and the name.

17. A — Reading many story books in your free time
   Extensive reading means reading widely.

18. A — So others can read them too
   It shows responsibility and fairness.

19. C — less
   Little, less, least.

20. A — delicious
   Delicious is a stronger, more exact word.

21. D — suddenly
   Time words show order.

22. C — Show a grown-up at once
   A trusted adult can help.

23. B — It was a trick to steal information
   The message asked for her name and address.

24. C — I do not have any money.
   Use any in negative sentences.

25. D — Everyone talks at once
   A club needs turn-taking so everyone is heard.

26. B — Re-reading the same passage several times
   Each re-reading improves speed and expression.

27. A — Reading parts from a script with only your voice, without costumes or sets
   Reader's theatre uses voices only.

28. C — She sings well.
   'Well' is the adverb; 'good' is an adjective.

29. A — never
   'Never' means at no time.

30. B — We bought rice, beans and maize.
   Commas separate items in a list and 'and' comes before the last.

31. A — Excuse me, may I ask a question?
   It is polite because it asks permission.

32. D — Drink plenty of safe water and see a health worker
   Drinking safe water and seeking help is important.

33. D — We swept the floor, and we wiped the desks.
   'And' adds an idea.

34. B — for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so
   The seven are remembered as FANBOYS.

35. C — The base form
   For example: 'When does she practise?'

36. B — Fixing a small problem early prevents a bigger one
   Early action saves later work.

37. B — written
   Write, wrote, written.

38. A — Money paid as a punishment for breaking a rule
   Fines punish law breaking.

39. A — into
   'Into' shows movement from outside to inside.

40. A — under
   'Under' shows where something is.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: A: Good morning, Ali. B: Good morning. A: May I borrow your book, please? B: Yes, here you are. A: Thank you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for greeting, request, answer and thanks.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Use it with an adult, keep your password secret, do not give your name or address to strangers, tell an adult if something frightens you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule, up to 4.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: The cake was as sweet as honey. The children danced like leaves in the wind.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each sentence with a correct simile.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Prevention means acting so that something bad does not happen. For example: Washing hands is a way of prevention.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the meaning, 1 for a sentence.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Open your mouth enough; speak slowly at first; listen to a good model and copy them; practise every day.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: b, a, c
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for b first and 1 mark for a then c.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: cow, dog, goat, hen
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for c and d first, 1 mark for g and h last.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: If they do not match, the listener may be confused about what you mean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for confusion and 1 for a clear reason.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Signs warn us of danger and tell us what to do, so misunderstanding one could cause an accident.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for what signs do and 1 mark for the danger of misunderstanding.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Manner: quietly, neatly. Time: later, always. Place: nearby, upstairs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct group.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: The children put loaves and tomatoes in the boxes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for children, loaves and tomatoes and boxes (award 3 for all correct).

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: A high rising voice shows surprise, while a low falling voice shows the speaker is not interested. So the tune of the voice shows feelings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way and 1 mark for linking to feelings.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sight, sound, smell, touch and taste. They help the reader to imagine the thing being described.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the senses and 1 for the reason.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'Hopping' means jumping, for example 'The rabbit is hopping.' 'Hoping' means wishing, for example 'I am hoping to win.'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for both sentences.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Energy foods such as ugali; body-building foods such as beans; protective foods such as spinach.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group with an example.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: gently, angrily, quickly
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty means returning what belongs to others. Neema returned the purse and refused a reward, and her mother said honesty is a great treasure.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for the example, 1 mark for the message.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: /uː/: food, spoon. /ʊ/: book, cook.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: running, sitting, swimming
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: Word stress is the syllable we say more strongly in a word, for example the first syllable in HOS-pi-tal.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for the example.

61. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: My sibling is my little sister. My aunt is a relative. My chore is to sweep the yard.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.
